claim: The Federal Reserve's official FOMC calendar page states the Committee holds eight regularly scheduled meetings during the year, and lists the exact 2021-2026 meeting dates (plus a 2027 preview) used verbatim, together with the historical archive pages for 2015-2020, as the hard-coded meeting-date list for the pre-FOMC drift candidates.
market_and_period: US, official Federal Reserve FOMC meeting calendar, 2021-2027 (current page); historical archive pages fomchistorical2015.htm through fomchistorical2020.htm supply 2015-2020 dates.
applicability: Grounds the exact, hard-coded FOMC_MEETINGS date list in scripts/screen_batches/h20260928_05_batch2.py, satisfying the brief's requirement that FOMC dates come from the Federal Reserve's own calendar pages, never inferred from price action.
limitations: The live page only shows 2021-2027; 2015-2020 dates were read from six separate historical archive pages (cited in the batch script's docstring), not re-snapshotted individually in this source-card set.
independent_replication: Federal Reserve historical archive pages (fomchistorical2015.htm..fomchistorical2020.htm) corroborate the same 8-meetings-per-year cadence for earlier years.
impact_on_spec: Freezes FOMC_MEETINGS as a literal, cited constant in the batch script; the two FOMC_DRIFT candidates cannot be tuned by choosing convenient meeting dates.

claim: S&P 500 Covered Call Fund Inc. (ticker BEP), the closed-end fund studied by Simon (2008)'s 'The Anomalous Behavior of the S&P Covered Call Closed End Fund,' liquidated on January 29, 2010 and distributed all proceeds to shareholders on February 2, 2010, per its own N-CSR annual report; the ticker is not tradable today, so XYLD is used as an honest live proxy for the same S&P 500 at-the-money monthly covered-call mechanism.
quote: The Fund liquidated on January 29, 2010 and distributed all proceeds to shareholders on February 2, 2010.
market_and_period: S&P 500 Covered Call Fund Inc. (BEP), closed-end fund, FY2009 N-CSR annual report, SEC EDGAR CIK 0001307155.
applicability: Confirms the registry's dir:covered_call_cef_income_pwb direction cannot be executed by literally holding BEP today; grounds the decision to substitute XYLD as an honest, cited proxy rather than silently inventing a ticker.
limitations: SEC filing confirms the fund's own liquidation, not the paper's replicated backtest numbers (26.60% CAGR / Sharpe 1.36 / -31.62% max drawdown claimed by paperswithbacktest are for a synthetic replication of the covered-call mechanism using SPX options over 1990-2026, not for holding the BEP shares themselves).
independent_replication: Cross-checked against a public web search (quantinvestor.wordpress.com, 2009-12-16 post) reporting the same Feb 2010 liquidation date before the filing was opened.
impact_on_spec: Justifies XYLD_COVERED_CALL_PROXY's universe (XYLD, not BEP) and requires the proxy be labeled honestly in the spec, source card and registry verdict rather than silently treated as a like-for-like replication.

claim: quantseeker.com's replication of the pre-FOMC announcement drift (Lucca & Moench 2015 Journal of Finance), tested on SPY through Dec 2024 plus leveraged ETFs, finds the drift remains persistent despite being published over a decade ago; the leveraged-ETF variant delivers an after-cost CAGR of 8-9% and a Sharpe ratio of about 0.6 while trading only 5% of the time (long from the close before a scheduled FOMC meeting through the close of its final day, cash otherwise).
quote: remains persistent despite being published over a decade ago
market_and_period: SPY EOD Jan 1993-Dec 2024, plus 1-min SPY Jan 2014-Dec 2024; QQQ/TQQQ/SPXL also tested, after 5bp one-way cost.
applicability: Grounds the FOMC_DRIFT_SPY / FOMC_DRIFT_TQQQ candidates' exact rule (entry at the close before a scheduled meeting, exit at the close of the final meeting day, cash otherwise) and its claimed after-cost performance.
limitations: Practitioner blog replication, not the original peer-reviewed paper; author's own backtest, not independently re-run by a third party in this pass; cost model (5bp) differs from this batch's 10/20bp screen_lane convention.
independent_replication: Builds on a peer-reviewed citation chain (Lucca & Moench 2015 JoF; Savor & Wilson 2013 JFQA; Cieslak, Morse & Vissing-Jorgensen 2019 JoF; Liu, Tang & Zhou 2022 JFE), per the registry's dir:pre_fomc_announcement_drift row.
impact_on_spec: Freezes the FOMC_DRIFT entry/exit convention (close-before-meeting to close-of-final-day) used by fomc_entry_dates/fomc_exit_dates in the batch script.

claim: Hull Tactical's replication of the turn-of-month effect (buy SPY at the close of the last trading day of the month, sell at the close of the 4th trading day of the next month, using Yahoo Finance SPY data) finds turn of the month captures 44% of the total return (before dividends) while invested roughly 20% of trading days.
quote: Turn of the month captures 44% of the total return (before dividends).
market_and_period: SPY (Yahoo Finance), turn-of-month window (last trading day of month through 4th trading day of the next month).
applicability: Grounds TOM_SPY's exact rule and holding-period definition (4th trading day, not 3rd or 5th) used by tom_signal_dates/w_tom_spy in the batch script.
limitations: Practitioner replication, before-dividends only; does not net out the batch's 10/20bp per-side cost convention; independent of but consistent with the registry's other four TOM sources (etftrends.com, alphainacademia.com x2, harbourfrontquant.substack.com).
independent_replication: etftrends.com's independent S&P 500 futures replication (1980-Q3 2024) reports the same qualitative underperformance-while-invested-fewer-days pattern; harbourfrontquant.substack.com's summary of a 2022 NTNU thesis reports the same turn-of-month effect persisting on individual-stock panels 1986-2021.
impact_on_spec: Freezes TOM_SPY's exact hold window (month-end close through the 4th trading day of the next month) in tom_signal_dates.

claim: Hedgefundie's Excellent Adventure (HFEA), a Bogleheads forum strategy since 2019, holds 55% UPRO / 45% TMF (updated in August 2019 from an original 40/60 UPRO/TMF risk-parity allocation) with quarterly rebalancing.
quote: Hedgefundie later updated the strategy's asset allocation in August 2019 to 55/45 UPRO/TMF. ... The proposed strategy calls for quarterly rebalancing.
market_and_period: UPRO (3x S&P 500) / TMF (3x 20+yr Treasury), since the 55/45 allocation was adopted in 2019-08.
applicability: Grounds HFEA_UPRO_TMF's exact fixed weights (55/45) and quarterly rebalance cadence in the batch script (approximated monthly in the lane, a documented conservative deviation -- more turnover than the published quarterly cadence).
limitations: Secondary summary of the primary Bogleheads forum thread (bogleheads.org/forum/viewtopic.php?t=272007), which returned a Cloudflare bot-challenge page when fetched directly in this session; optimizedportfolio.com's summary is used as an independent, dated secondary source instead. Does not itself report a post-cost Sharpe for the frozen windows used here.
independent_replication: The Bogleheads forum thread itself (viewtopic.php?t=272007, and its continuation Part II at viewtopic.php?t=288192) is the primary community record; optimizedportfolio.com's summary is consistent with the widely-cited 55/45 quarterly-rebalance description used across other practitioner write-ups of HFEA found in this pass's web search.
impact_on_spec: Freezes HFEA_UPRO_TMF's exact fixed weights (55% UPRO / 45% TMF) in the batch script's HFEA candidate definition.

claim: Graziani (2024, SSRN, 'Time Series Reversal: An End-of-the-Month Perspective'), summarized by harbourfrontquant.substack.com: S&P 500 end-of-month returns (4th Friday to month-end) are negatively correlated with the following month's return; a simple trading strategy based on this effect (buy next month iff end-of-month return was negative) outperforms buy-and-hold over a 45-year period.
quote: end-of-month returns of the S&P 500 are negatively correlated with returns one month later ... a simple trading strategy based on this effect...outperforms the buy-and-hold strategy over a 45-year period.
market_and_period: S&P 500, 45-year period per the secondary summary (primary SSRN paper not independently opened in this session).
applicability: Grounds EOM_REVERSAL_SPY's exact signal (sign of the 4th-Friday-to-month-end return) and long/cash rule used by w_eom_reversal_spy in the batch script.
limitations: Secondary summary of the primary SSRN paper (not independently opened in this session); gives no CAGR/Sharpe/drawdown numbers, only a qualitative outperformance claim over an unspecified 45-year sample ending before this substack post's 2025-04-14 publish date. Does not net out the batch's 10/20bp per-side cost convention.
independent_replication: Not independently replicated in this pass beyond the single harbourfrontquant.substack.com secondary source; distinguished in direction-review.json from the turn-of-month/turn-of-quarter/turn-of-year cluster summarized in the same post (a different, non-contrarian mechanism).
impact_on_spec: Freezes EOM_REVERSAL_SPY's exact signal (4th-Friday-to-month-end SPY return sign) and single calendar-anchored decision date, which drove the 2026-09-28 freq_correction (declared single-version 'D' instead of a 21-offset monthly sweep).

claim: Quantpedia's 'Front-Running Seasonality in US Stock Sectors': shifting the seasonal-ranking month one month earlier than the literal same-calendar-month-last-year rank ('front-running'), then holding the top 2 of 9 Select Sector SPDRs equal-weight, monthly rebalance, outperforms the benchmark particularly since 2009 with a higher Sharpe and Calmar ratio than the benchmark despite higher volatility.
quote: at the end of December, an investor selects ETFs for January by assessing their performance from the previous February ... the strategy achieved the best results by holding two ETFs in long positions ... rebalance monthly ... outperforms the benchmark, particularly since 2009 [with] a more favorable Sharpe Ratio ... higher Calmar Ratio.
market_and_period: 9 Select Sector SPDRs (XLB/XLE/XLF/XLI/XLK/XLP/XLU/XLV/XLY), tested 2000-11-01..2023-11-01 per the page's Figure 2.
applicability: Grounds FRONT_RUN_SECTOR_TOP2's exact rule: one-month-earlier-shifted seasonal ranking, top-2-of-9 equal-weight, monthly rebalance -- the source's own best-performing (highest Sharpe/Calmar) variant, used unmodified in the batch script.
limitations: Author's own claimed performance is described in the article's own tables/charts (not independently re-derived by Quantpedia's methodology text alone); no realistic transaction-cost assumption is given in the excerpt fetched. This session fetched the live quantpedia.com page directly (equivalent content to the 2025-02-15 web.archive.org snapshot originally cited in direction-review.json, both showing the 2024-12-19 publish date).
independent_replication: Not independently replicated by a second source in this pass; the related futures/commodity version (AllocateSmartly's 'Front Running Commodity Seasonality', the article this piece is explicitly modeled on) is out of scope (commodities/futures, not ETFs we trade).
impact_on_spec: Freezes FRONT_RUN_SECTOR_TOP2's exact rule (one-month-early-shifted seasonal rank, top-2-of-9, monthly), which drove the 2026-09-28 freq_correction (declared single-version 'D' instead of a 21-offset monthly sweep since the score is only defined at month-end).
